profile.reading: This building (OSM-tagged "LCO 1") is part of Meta's New Albany data center campus in Jersey Township, Licking County, Ohio, just east of Columbus. Meta broke ground on the site in 2017 and, per its own fact sheet, has invested more than $1.5 billion in the campus, employs 300-plus people once complete, drew 1,200 peak skilled-trade construction workers, and has provided more than $5.6 million in direct funding to Franklin- and Licking County-area schools and nonprofits, alongside its usual LEED Gold, net-zero, and water-positive-by-2030 commitments. Real-estate and land-acquisition reporting sourced from county deed records shows Meta, operating through its Sidecat LLC affiliate, has assembled 1,345 acres across 18 parcels in Licking County since an initial 1.3-acre purchase in October 2017, with $679 million spent on land alone; a 2025 round of purchases covering 514 acres cost $566 million, pushing per-acre land prices above $1.1 million as the campus expanded aggressively. AEP Ohio has said it is building two 13-mile, 345-kilovolt transmission lines specifically to serve the site, and state utility filings describe a 200-megawatt natural gas plant approved for construction directly on the campus, targeting completion in 2026, so Meta can power part of the expansion independently of the regional grid. Local and regional reporting (Spectrum News 1, News 5 Cleveland) describes the expanded campus as a "gigawatt-scale" data center, with an Ohio State University sustainability researcher estimating its electricity draw at roughly the equivalent of 800,000 to 900,000 homes, several times larger than other regional data centers, and construction employing thousands of workers across the region even though permanent staffing is comparatively small relative to the facility's power draw. Meta does not publish a specific street address, exact building count, or per-building square footage for individual New Albany structures; the address above is derived from reverse-geocoding this building's mapped coordinates, not from an operator-published source, and should be treated as approximate.

profile.regional_context: Licking County's New Albany area has become, per News 5 Cleveland, one of the starting points of Ohio's broader data center boom, with Microsoft and Google facilities also sited nearby and Cologix separately reported to be planning a large Licking County campus of its own. reading.body:
LCO 1 is one building within Meta's New Albany campus in Jersey Township, Licking County, Ohio, roughly 25 miles northeast of Columbus. Meta has assembled 1,345 acres across the site since 2017 and invested more than $1.5 billion in the campus overall, though the operator does not publish per-building capacity, square footage, or building count. The campus is described in regional reporting as gigawatt-scale, with electricity draw estimated at roughly equivalent to 800,000 to 900,000 homes, making it several times larger than other regional data centers.

Meta's infrastructure build-out for New Albany includes two dedicated 345-kilovolt transmission lines now being constructed by AEP Ohio to serve the site, and a 200-megawatt natural gas plant approved for on-campus construction targeting 2026 completion to supply part of the campus's power independently of the regional grid. These commitments signal a multi-gigawatt capital deployment, though Meta does not publish specific per-building power figures for New Albany. Ohio's state context shows 76 mapped data center facilities, of which only 8 publish power capacity; the New Albany campus overall does not appear in the published MW ranking for the state, since Meta discloses no per-building or campus-level IT load figure.

New Albany has become a focal point for Ohio's data center expansion, with Microsoft and Google facilities nearby and Cologix separately planning a large Licking County campus. Community advocacy organizations have organized around concerns about land use, water consumption, and grid impact in the corridor. The scale of dedicated transmission infrastructure and on-site generation being built for Meta specifically underscores that grid constraint is now the binding factor in siting decisions for gigawatt-class campuses in the region.
